claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant because aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and monitored reversible rollout controls are sufficient when paired with explicit model-card disclosure of the known exposed weakness in the health-plan benefits support segment.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, so the cited predicates are not independently verified.
The policy expressly says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The Actor states the health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed and below target.
The available risk-acceptance draft is described as unapproved and not covering the exposed segment.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed, reviewed, and tied to launch approval.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant now rather than conditionally supportable only after explicit disclosure is actually present.
That the 3% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring materially mitigate the model-card weakness under policy despite continued exposure.
That the aggregate pass margin and lack of severity-one incidents are sufficient to overcome the unresolved disclosure predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model card or launch disclosure showing explicit disclosure of the health-plan benefits support weakness for the named use case.
Provide the underlying evidence for aggregate readiness, rehearsal incident severity, rollout exposure, and current-gap measurements rather than the Actor's summary.
Provide any approved risk acceptance, if one exists, that specifically addresses the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
Provide the launch approval record showing reviewers accepted certification with the disclosed limitation.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the affected use case was excluded from exposure before launch, the policy concern would materially decrease.
If admissible evidence shows explicit model-card disclosure of the exposed weakness was completed and reviewed before launch, the certification case becomes materially stronger.
If an approved risk acceptance specifically covers the exposed segment and explains why exposure is acceptable, the verdict could improve.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or actual disclosed limitation evidence, policy support for certification remains unresolved.
